exposure: Infants with different genetic subtypes of PWS
cohort: 244 infants with Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) and 365 healthy infants
finding: Infants with PWS had a higher prevalence of maternal age over 35, polyhydramnios, cesarean section, labor induction, breech presentation, decreased fetal movements, hypotonia, cryptorchidism, poor sucking, and lower birth weight compared to healthy infants.
mod_finding: The study found a higher prevalence of cesarean section births in infants with Prader-Willi syndrome compared to healthy infants.
birth_weight: Lower in infants with PWS compared to healthy infants
